purpose: Determine whether three below-ground cores can sample within-node Thalassia spatial heterogeneity without selecting core positions using TNC values or any future response.

source.geometry_registry: Pinned 2023-2025 recent Tampa meter-mark reconstruction already used by analysis/55_bare_control_spatial_preflight.py

frozen_anchor_rule.if_three_or_more_positive_marks: sort Thalassia-positive site_m and choose observed marks nearest the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles; ties -> lower site_m; require three unique anchors where possible
frozen_anchor_rule.if_two_positive_marks: one anchor at each positive mark; third independent core is assigned to the positive mark closest to the midpoint between the two and uses a separately frozen lateral/perpendicular offset
frozen_anchor_rule.if_one_positive_mark: all three independent cores are placed adjacent to the single positive mark using three pre-frozen non-overlapping offsets
frozen_anchor_rule.destructive_sampling: never core directly on the permanent meter mark; core-offset geometry must be frozen before field collection

primary_node_summary: median rhizome TNC across the three valid independent cores
claim_boundary: This uses already-open recent vegetation state for sampling feasibility only.
Core positions are chosen from baseline Thalassia geometry, not TNC values or the future outcome.
A sparse node with one or two positive marks remains eligible but provides less within-node spatial coverage; report this design class.
Do not relocate cores after assay results are known.
